headline: Calm greed holds as markets await Nvidia earnings and inflation data
body: Equities enter Wednesday in a holding pattern after three straight winning sessions pushed the S&P 500 to roughly 7,677 and the Dow to a fresh closing high near 53,577. Futures are essentially flat to slightly lower, with the Nasdaq 100 lagging as traders trim risk ahead of Nvidia's earnings report after the close -- still the single most consequential print for the AI trade. The CNN Fear & Greed gauge sits in the mid-to-high 50s (Greed), and the VIX recently touched a 2026 low near 14, signs of a market that is content rather than euphoric: positioning has drifted toward optimism, but few want to make a big directional bet hours before the catalyst.

The macro backdrop is doing more waiting than moving. The Fed has held its target range at 3.50%-3.75% since July, and markets have pushed easing expectations out toward 2027 as inflation cools only gradually; today's core PCE reading, expected roughly steady near 3.3%, is the next data point that could shift that timeline. Treasury yields have eased and oil has extended its slide, taking some pressure off rate-sensitive sectors. Retail chatter leans more idiosyncratic than directional -- social trackers show heavy mention volume around Nvidia, Alphabet and SpaceX alongside renewed meme-stock spikes in names like GameStop, suggesting speculative appetite is alive but scattered rather than a coordinated market-wide signal.
